title: Mean below target during bribery
statement: Let $n>0$, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, and let $\tau\in\mathbb R$. Starting with $J_0=\varnothing$, construct $J_{k+1}$ from $J_k$ by adding a coordinate of maximum influence for the function obtained from $f$ by setting all coordinates in $J_k$ to $1$ if that function's mean is below $\tau$; otherwise leave the set unchanged. If $t\le n$ and the set $J_n$ has cardinality greater than $t$, then the mean of the function obtained by setting the coordinates in $J_t$ to $1$ is strictly less than $\tau$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$t$ is a natural number with $t\le n$
The recursively constructed set $J_n$ has cardinality greater than $t$
